title: StorageClasses & Dynamic Provisioning
summary: Let PVCs create their own PVs: StorageClass fields, binding modes, the default class and volume expansion.

blocks.text: A StorageClass describes a **class** of storage an admin offers, such as a quality-of-service level or backup policy. Kubernetes doesn't care what the classes mean. Users pick one **by name**, so the name matters.

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: <class-name>
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "false"
provisioner: <provisioner-name>
reclaimPolicy: Retain          # default is Delete
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - <option>
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  <key>: "<value>"            # provider-specific
`provisioner`, `parameters` and `reclaimPolicy` are used when a PV of this class has to be **dynamically provisioned** for a PVC.

rows: **Required.** Which volume plugin provisions PVs. Internal ones are prefixed `kubernetes.io`; external provisioners (e.g. for NFS) are separate programs.
Provider-specific. Omitted ones get a default. At most **512** parameters, **256 KiB** in total.
`Delete` or `Retain`; **defaults to Delete**. Manually created PVs keep whatever policy they were given.
`true` lets users grow a PV by editing its PVC. You can only **grow**, never shrink.
Copied to dynamically provisioned PVs. Not validated; if the plugin doesn't support them, provisioning fails.

blocks.text: `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner` marks a class that can't provision automatically, as with `local` volumes. The class still exists to delay binding.

items: **Immediate**: binding and provisioning happen as soon as the PVC is created, without knowing where the Pod will run. With topology-constrained storage (not reachable from every node) this can leave Pods **unschedulable**.

**WaitForFirstConsumer**: waits until a Pod using the PVC is created, then picks or provisions a PV that fits the Pod's scheduling constraints (resource requests, node selectors, affinity/anti-affinity, taints and tolerations).
WaitForFirstConsumer is supported for dynamic provisioning by CSI drivers that support it, and for pre-created `local` PVs.
`allowedTopologies` can still restrict provisioning to given zones if needed.

blocks.text: With WaitForFirstConsumer, **don't** set `nodeName` in the Pod: it bypasses the scheduler and the PVC stays **Pending**. Use a `nodeSelector` on `kubernetes.io/hostname` instead.
Without it, admins must create storage at the provider and then a PV for it. With it, storage is created **on demand** when a user creates a PVC.

items: The admin creates one or more StorageClasses (API group `storage.k8s.io`), each naming a provisioner and its parameters.
The user sets `storageClassName` on the PVC to the class name. The old `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` annotation is deprecated.
The provisioner creates the volume and a PV, which is bound to the claim. In the docs' example, deleting the claim **destroys the volume** (the default Delete policy).

To provision **every** claim that names no class: mark one StorageClass as default **and** enable the `DefaultStorageClass` admission controller on the API server. It fills in `storageClassName` on new PVCs.

blocks.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: <pvc-name>
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: <class-name>
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: <size>

items: A PVC with **no** `storageClassName` gets the default StorageClass.
If several classes are marked default, the **most recently created** one is used. Aim for only one; multiple defaults exist to allow seamless migration.
A cluster may have no default. A PVC created then keeps its class unset, and is updated **retroactively** when a default appears.
A PVC with `storageClassName: ""` is **not** updated; it keeps binding only to PVs with no class.

blocks.text: Your installer may create a default class that doesn't suit you (too expensive, for example). Deleting it may not work, because an addon manager can re-create it. Change the annotation instead.

kubectl get storageclass          # the default shows "(default)"

# 1. un-default the current one
kubectl patch storageclass <old> -p '{"metadata": {"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"false"}}}'

# 2. make another the default
kubectl patch storageclass <new> -p '{"metadata": {"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}'

items: Only the value `true` makes a class default. Any other value, or no annotation, counts as false.
A PVC with `volumeName` stays pending if the static PV's `storageClassName` doesn't match the PVC's class.

blocks.text: Memorize the annotation `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` and the `kubectl patch storageclass` form above. Check the result with `kubectl get storageclass`.

items: Only possible when the PVC's StorageClass has `allowVolumeExpansion: true`. Supported for `csi` (the CSI driver must support it), plus deprecated `flexVolume` and `portworxVolume`.
To expand, **edit the PVC** and request a larger size. The existing volume is resized; **no new PV** is created.
File systems can only be resized if they are **XFS, Ext3 or Ext4**. The resize happens when a Pod uses the PVC in ReadWrite mode.
An in-use PVC is expanded without recreating the Pod. A PVC no Pod uses won't finish expanding until a Pod uses it.
If the requested size is too big for the backend, the resize is retried until someone acts, for example by requesting a smaller size.

blocks.text: Don't edit the **PV's** capacity by hand. If you then set the PVC to the same size, the control plane assumes the volume was already resized and no resize happens.

questions.stem: A PVC sets `storageClassName: fast`. What does that value have to match?

options.text: The name of a StorageClass created by the administrator
options.explanation: The class is chosen by name.
The PVC names the class; the class names the provisioner.
Labels are matched with a selector, not storageClassName.

questions.stem: A StorageClass doesn't set `reclaimPolicy`. What policy do its dynamically provisioned PVs get?
In a multi-zone cluster, a zonal disk is provisioned as soon as the PVC is created, and the Pod later can't be scheduled. Which setting avoids this?

options.explanation: Provisioning then follows the Pod's scheduling constraints.
That's the default that caused the problem.
Controls what happens after the PVC is deleted.

questions.stem: A Pod uses a PVC whose class has WaitForFirstConsumer, and sets `nodeName` in its spec. The PVC stays Pending. Why?

options.text: nodeName bypasses the scheduler, so binding never happens; use a nodeSelector on kubernetes.io/hostname
The class must be the default
The reclaim policy must be Retain

questions.stem: Which are needed so that PVCs with no storageClassName get dynamically provisioned? Select 2.

options.text: The DefaultStorageClass admission controller enabled on the API server
options.explanation: It adds storageClassName to new PVCs.

options.text: A PV pre-created for every PVC

questions.stem: Which command makes the StorageClass `gold` the default?

options.explanation: Defaulting uses an annotation with a specific key, not a label.
That edits a PVC, not the default class.

questions.stem: True or false: If two StorageClasses are both marked default, creating a PVC without storageClassName fails.

options.explanation: Kubernetes uses the most recently created default.
Correct — multiple defaults are allowed to ease migration, though one is recommended.

questions.stem: Why might deleting the pre-installed default StorageClass not be a good way to disable it?

options.text: An addon manager may re-create it automatically
options.explanation: The task page warns about this; patch the annotation instead.
They can; the problem is re-creation.

options.text: All PVs of the class are deleted too
kubectl refuses to delete the default class

questions.stem: A PVC has `storageClassName: ""`. An admin then adds a default StorageClass. What happens to the PVC?

options.text: Nothing: it keeps requesting PVs with no class
options.explanation: Only PVCs with the field unset are updated retroactively.

options.text: It is updated to the new default
options.explanation: That only happens when storageClassName is unset.
An empty class opts out of dynamic provisioning.

questions.stem: A user edits a PVC to request more storage, but nothing happens and the class doesn't allow it. Which StorageClass field is missing?
True or false: Expanding a PVC creates a new, larger PersistentVolume and copies the data.

options.explanation: No new PV is created; the existing volume is resized.

questions.stem: Which statements about volume expansion are true? Select 2.

options.text: You can grow a volume but not shrink it
options.explanation: Stated on the Storage Classes page.

options.text: It's enabled per class with allowVolumeExpansion
options.explanation: The underlying StorageClass must allow it.

options.text: It works for every volume type
options.explanation: Only listed types (e.g. CSI) support it.

questions.stem: You need a StorageClass for pre-created `local` PVs. Which settings match the docs?

options.explanation: Local volumes have no dynamic provisioning, but binding should wait for the Pod.

options.text: A real provisioner with volumeBindingMode: Immediate
options.explanation: Local volumes don't support dynamic provisioning, and Immediate ignores Pod placement.

options.text: No StorageClass is ever needed for local volumes
options.explanation: The docs say a class should still be created to delay binding.
